title: Round 30 Virginia-West Virginia state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for Virginia and West Virginia. Every seeded row reproduces one USGS GNIS record screened by exact official name, returned type/state/county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned GNIS primary point, and cross-checked on two independent USGS surfaces (USGS GNIS Geocoder; staged-products DomesticNames text via tools/gnis_extract.py; cumulative candidate extract resources/city-subsurface/gnis-candidates-batch7.json with per-state ZIP SHA-256 values). Mount Rogers and Spruce Knob additionally carry Domestic Names per-ID identity checks. Six batch-13 rows are Virginia independent cities whose county identities differ in spelling between the two surfaces; the Shenandoah/New cross-state river decisions and the Kanawha county preservation are recorded below.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature and the point lay inside the intended state. County/census divisions, historical places, and same-name records of another class or county were rejected explicitly where relevant.

gnisDomesticNames.use: Second-surface cross-check of every seeded FEATURE_ID and per-ID identity checks for Mount Rogers (1485637) and Spruce Knob (1553014), extracted in a GitHub Actions runner by tools/gnis_extract.py. The current text layout carries no elevation columns, so the two summit elevations cite USGS-published state-highpoint values. The text file keys Virginia independent cities as '<name> (city)'; verification normalizes that suffix against the Geocoder's 'City of <name>' form rather than editing either surface. The candidate extract file is cumulative across batches 7-13; this register is the frozen batch-13 evidence.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service, reproduced identically on the second USGS surface.

Grouped Geocoder Types map explicitly to stored row classes: Cities & Populated Places to Populated Place, Lakes & Reservoirs to Lake for the accepted named lakes and reservoirs (the extract's text class for the batch-13 lake rows is Reservoir), Streams & Canals to Stream, and Summit to Summit.
A stored GNIS primary point is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline polygon, summit outline, or river centerline.

If exact-name candidates remain indistinguishable, or the state-filtered screen returns no intended feature record, the feature is omitted from that state gazetteer and may appear only as a generalized context corridor.
Statewide frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized corridors; no bundled DEM or surveyed boundary is implied.

virginia.title: Virginia statewide frame (Virginia-West Virginia batch)
virginia.frameNote: Virginia-West Virginia batch: the Richmond capital anchor (an independent city) is balanced with the per-ID Mount Rogers high point, three reservoirs (Smith Mountain, Anna, Claytor), six independent-city/county-seat rows, and two river mouth records (James, Rappahannock). The Shenandoah and New Rivers return no Virginia stream records (their GNIS records are West Virginia-associated and seeded there); the Potomac is a corridor (Maryland/DC-associated record).

identityDecisions.candidate: Virginia independent cities (Richmond, Virginia Beach, Norfolk, Roanoke, Charlottesville, Chesapeake)
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded with county field 'City of <name>', the Geocoder's verbatim county string; the DomesticNames text keys the same FEATURE_IDs to '<name> (city)'. Both surfaces denote the independent city; verification normalizes the two surface spellings (as with Saint Louis, MO, in batch 11) rather than editing either. Same-name county records (Richmond County, Roanoke County) are not seeded.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The points are not municipal boundaries.

identityDecisions.candidate: Spruce Knob, FEATURE_ID 1555698 (Randolph County) and Spruce Knob Lake 1553015
identityDecisions.decision: Rejected. Two West Virginia summits share the name; the seeded Pendleton County record 1553014 matches the published state-highpoint location (4,863 ft).
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The seeded point is not a surveyed summit outline.

identityDecisions.candidate: Shenandoah River and New River stream records
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded in West Virginia. The Shenandoah's mouth record is at Harpers Ferry (WV) and the New's confluence record is in Fayette County, WV; under states=VA both names return no stream record (Shenandoah: subdivision records only; New: a populated place/CDP). Both rivers remain corridors in Virginia.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The mouth points are not channel centerlines or state boundaries.

identityDecisions.candidate: Kanawha River primary county Fayette (mouth point at Point Pleasant)
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded with the county both surfaces return (Fayette), preserved verbatim rather than 'corrected' to the mouth county (Mason). GNIS keys the multi-county record to its source-reach county; the point, class, and name reproduce exactly on both surfaces, and the point is geographically coherent (Ohio confluence). Recorded so future readers do not mistake it for a transcription error.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The county string is not a claim that the mouth point lies in Fayette County.

identityDecisions.candidate: Ohio River and Monongahela River under states=WV
identityDecisions.decision: Empty screens. The Ohio main stem is Kentucky-associated (seeded in Kentucky, batch 12); the Monongahela is Pennsylvania-associated (seeded in Pennsylvania, batch 10). Both remain corridors in West Virginia.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The corridors are not channel centerlines or state boundaries.

identityDecisions.candidate: Potomac River under states=VA; Lynchburg, Harrisonburg, and Kerr Lake
identityDecisions.decision: The Potomac screen returned an empty array (its record belongs to the MD/DC reach) and remains a corridor. Identity-safe candidates omitted under the starter-scope treatment.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: Starter-scope omission is not a claim about feature importance or identity.

knownLimitations: Virginia and West Virginia are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.

The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; exact-match screening by name/type/state/county/FEATURE_ID is part of the evidence. Every seeded row was reproduced on the second USGS surface (staged-products DomesticNames text) at the same primary point; county spellings are normalized only for the independent-city suffix/abbreviation differences recorded above.

The current DomesticNames text layout carries no elevation columns, so Mount Rogers (5,729 feet) and Spruce Knob (4,863 feet) elevations cite USGS-published state-highpoint values; GNIS identity rests on the per-ID class/county/point reproduction.
GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain or corridors. Both frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context lines.
State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks. Both rectangles include areas outside their state outlines; no boundary geometry is claimed.
